stories.title: Arrow Arranges $85M Construction Loan for Miami Condo Project
stories.excerpt: Arrow Real Estate Advisors arranged an $85 million construction loan on behalf of Northlink Capital for the development of 7200 Collins Avenue, a 222-unit luxury condominium project in Miami Beach, Florida. The financing, provided by Deutsche Bank, refinances existing debt and will fund the ground-up construction of the 12-story, 274,150-square-foot residential tower through completion. Located at the intersection of Collins Avenue and 72nd Street in Miami Beach’s North Beach neighborhood, the project will offer a collection of studio-, one-, and two-bedroom residences with an average unit size of approximately 489 square feet. Approximately 81% of the residences are priced below $1 million. Amenities will span three levels and include the exclusive 7200 Collins Beach Club, a swimming pool, fitness center, ground-floor retail and food and beverage offerings, and landscaped rooftop sundecks. Arrow Real Estate Advisors’ Morris Betesh, Alex Bailkin, and Matt O’Hanlon arranged the financing. bullets: Deutsche Bank arranged $85M construction loan for 222-unit Miami Beach luxury condo
81% of units priced below $1M; 12-story tower in North Beach neighborhood

stories.summary: Arrow Real Estate Advisors arranged an $85 million construction loan from Deutsche Bank for Northlink Capital's 7200 Collins Avenue, a 222-unit luxury condominium project in Miami Beach's North Beach. The 12-story, 274,150-square-foot tower offers studio, one-, and two-bedroom residences with an average unit size of 489 square feet; 81% of units are priced below $1 million. Financing refinances existing debt and funds ground-up construction through completion.
stories.impact: Miami Beach condo market shows sustained financing appetite for luxury for-sale product despite broader credit tightness. Below-$1M unit pricing signals developer confidence in demand from downsizers and primary-residence buyers, not speculative investment, which steers capital away from rental multifamily. This reinforces Miami's bifurcated market: condo capital remains available while rental development may face tighter underwriting.

stories.title: Richman Group, Monadnock Plan to Build 420 Units in East Harlem
stories.excerpt: Get a little place in Harlem and you’ll figure it out. Developers Richman Group and Monadnock Development — in a joint venture — have filed plans with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) to construct a 420-unit residential building at 243 East 125th Street in Manhattan’s East Harlem neighborhood. The plan, which was filed July 26 by Richman Group President Kristin Miller, calls for the construction of a 14-story mixed-use building with 648,000 square feet of residential space, 82,000 square feet of commercial space and a 10,700-square-foot community facility. Construction is scheduled to begin by early 2027. Paul Carr of S9 Architecture is the registered architect on the project. Spokespeople for S9 Architecture, Richman Group and Monadnock Development did not immediately respond to requests for comment. If approved, the building’s second through 14th floors would each include between 28 and 38 apartments, according to the DOB plans. The plans also note there will be 65 parking spaces, plus a lot attendant on staff, and bicycle storage for 218 bikes. In addition, the developers are planning for two retail spaces, a social services office, and amenities including a lounge, a gym, a kids playroom and a multipurpose room. The building, on the corner of 125th Street and Second Avenue, would be part of the New York City Economic Development Corporation’s B-East (East 125th Street Development project), a 17,337-square-foot, city-owned property where the city aims to add more mixed-income housing. B-East is part of the broader East 125th Street Development project first approved in 2008, which will ultimately build housing on three land parcels and include about 1.7 million square feet of residential, retail and commercial development. Since the project launched, it has already delivered 451 housing units — including 344 affordable units — and 65,000 square feet of retail space. stories.impact: East Harlem rental pipeline growth signals sustained developer confidence in East Harlem's gentrification arc and market-rate demand. Early 2027 start means delivery likely 2029–2030, placing this asset ahead of anticipated peak supply in Lower East Side/East Village submarkets. The community-facility component suggests public subsidy or tax incentive participation, indicating NYC's continued reliance on density to absorb workforce housing needs—watch for zoning or PILOT details affecting project economics.

stories.title: Vital Infrastructure REIT Buys East New York Outpatient Facility for $90M
stories.excerpt: A Toronto-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has purchased an East New York, Brooklyn, medical facility for $89.9 million. Health care infrastructure REIT Vital Infrastructure Property Trust announced last week that it acquired the 142,249-square-foot East New York Health Hub at 101 Pennsylvania Avenue, which is leased as an outpatient care facility to AdvantageCare Physicians New York. Newmark’s Ben Appel, Adam Spies, Jay Miele, Justin Shepherd, John Nero, Adam Doneger, Matt Berres, Michael Greeley, Ron Ott, Conor Hilton and Drew Martin negotiated on behalf of the buyer and the seller, according to Crain’s New York Business. The seller is Squarefeet.com owner Jonas Rudofsky, a former Newmark director, who has owned the property since 2019, when it was first developed, according to property records. “This acquisition represents another important step in the execution of Vital Infrastructure’s growth strategy,” Zach Vaughan, CEO of Vital Infrastructure, said in a statement. “East New York Health Hub is a modern, institutional-quality, multi-disciplinary health care facility located in a high-barrier market and leased to one of New York’s largest health care networks. The acquisition further strengthens the resilience and quality of our portfolio while expanding our presence in a key U.S. market.” The Newmark team declined to comment. Newmark, however, identified the tenant as nonprofit insurance company EmblemHealth, while Vital said that AdvantageCare still has 11 years remaining on its lease. The building is also leased to New York Cancer & Blood Specialists, Lenox Hill Radiology, New York Health, Advanced Dermatology and Quest Diagnostics, according to the buyer. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vital Infrastructure REIT acquired 142,249 sq ft East New York medical facility for $89.9M
101 Pennsylvania Avenue leased to AdvantageCare Physicians New York as outpatient care hub

stories.summary: Vital Infrastructure Property Trust, a Toronto-based healthcare REIT, acquired the East New York Health Hub at 101 Pennsylvania Avenue in Brooklyn for $89.9 million. The 142,249-square-foot facility is leased to AdvantageCare Physicians New York as an outpatient care facility. The property was originally developed in 2019 and was sold by Jonas Rudofsky, former Newmark director.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, healthcare facility anchoring in East New York/Cypress Hills indicates infrastructure investment and job creation in a high-growth, affordable-housing-pressure submarket. This signals institutional capital confidence in the neighborhood's residential absorption and affordability-constrained rental market, potentially supporting rents and forward-looking multifamily development feasibility in the micromarket.

stories.title: Stewards Inks $79M Refi of Hollywood Rental Asset
stories.excerpt: Stewards Inc. completed a $79 million refinancing of 1818 Park, its luxury multifamily residential community in downtown Hollywood, Florida. Multihousing News reports Stewards acquired 1818 Park last August for $190 million. 1818 Park is a 22-story luxury residential community offering studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom residences complemented by resort-style amenities, including coworking space, fitness facilities, resort-style pools and ground-floor retail. The property is currently approximately 94% occupied and benefits from its location in downtown Hollywood. The refinancing was completed with senior financing provided by Värde Partners and mezzanine financing provided by CCL Capital. The transaction was arranged by BayBridge Real Estate Capital, with Jay Miller, Spencer Miller, AJ Felberbaum and Noah Rothman leading the placement effort on behalf of the Company. On its website, Stewards touts that its integrated model combines technology-enabled small business finance, income-producing real estate, and emerging digital infrastructure, creating a diversified foundation for performance, stability, and scale. The property is currently 94% occupied and was acquired by Stewards in August 2023 for $190 million. Senior financing came from Värde Partners and mezzanine financing from CCL Capital, arranged by BayBridge Real Estate Capital.
stories.impact: Refi at 41.6% LTV on a $190M August 2023 acquisition signals strong operational performance and stable cap rates in South Florida luxury rental market. High occupancy (94%) and successful refi in current rate environment demonstrate coastal Florida multifamily demand resilience. This validates development risk assumptions for premium assets in downtown Hollywood submarket and suggests cap-rate compression may be stabilizing—relevant for forward-looking acquisitions.

stories.title: White Lodging Breaks Ground on Marriott-Branded Charlotte Hotel
stories.excerpt: White Lodging will break ground this month on a new Autograph Collection (Marriott) hotel in Charlotte’s South End neighborhood, marking the company’s fifth Autograph property in its national portfolio of more than 60 hotels. Situated at the intersection of South Tryon Street and Bland Street, the project is the first full-service hotel in the South End. The 295-room luxury hotel will feature nearly 10,000 square feet of meeting space and a ground-floor restaurant. Amenities include an open-air pool deck on the hotel’s fifth floor, a public steam sauna, plus cold- and hot-plunge pools and a spa. A restaurant and bar at the hotel has been designed to serve as a community anchor in the South End neighborhood. Brasfield & Gorrie is in charge of construction and Abeyta Architecture Studio & Corgan Architects are designing the project. stories.summary: White Lodging is breaking ground on a new Autograph Collection (Marriott) hotel in Charlotte's South End neighborhood, the company's fifth Autograph property nationally. The 295-room luxury hotel will feature nearly 10,000 square feet of meeting space, a ground-floor restaurant, an open-air pool deck, spa, and plunge pools. The project is the first full-service hotel in the South End.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. However, hospitality anchor in Charlotte South End signals neighborhood densification and amenity proliferation that typically precedes or accompanies mixed-use residential development. Ground-floor restaurant and resort positioning suggest strong urban walkability positioning in South End, which supports rental multifamily demand and rent growth in the micromarket over next 2–3 years.

stories.title: EM Debt Emerges as Top Relative-Value Play for Yield
stories.excerpt: Executive Summary Emerging market debt is regaining momentum after a three-year capital flight, with more than $17 billion of net inflows so far this year and improving sovereign credit quality supporting the case for both hard-currency and local-currency strategies. The trade remains sensitive to the U.S. dollar and geopolitics, but it is a compelling way to capture income, diversification and potential spread compression. Relative-Value Play Emerging market debt is reemerging as one of the strongest relative-value opportunities in global fixed income, as institutional investors rotate toward higher-yielding sovereign and corporate bonds amid improving credit conditions and slowing inflation across many developing economies. The asset class has reversed course following three consecutive years of capital outflows between 2022 and 2024. During the past 15 months, investor sentiment has improved markedly, with emerging market bond funds attracting more than $17 billion in net inflows this year. While emerging market debt still carries currency and geopolitical risks, the combination of attractive real yields, improving sovereign credit quality and portfolio diversification has strengthened its appeal relative to many developed-market fixed-income assets. Higher Real Rates Stand Out The widening gap in real interest rates between emerging and developed economies makes this trade a compelling one. Central banks in countries including Brazil, Colombia, Indonesia and Egypt tightened monetary policy aggressively during the global inflation cycle. As inflation has since moderated while policy rates remain elevated, one can now earn some of the highest inflation-adjusted yields available in global bond markets. By contrast, many developed economies continue to contend with persistent inflation, leaving real returns on government debt comparatively less attractive despite higher nominal yields. Emerging market corporate bonds also continue to offer a meaningful yield premium
bullets: Emerging market debt attracting $17B+ net inflows in 2024 after three years of capital flight
Institutional investor rotation toward higher-yielding sovereign and corporate bonds in developing economies
Improving credit quality, slowing inflation, and real-yield advantages drive EM fixed-income appeal
stories.summary: Emerging market debt is experiencing renewed investor appetite following three consecutive years of capital outflows between 2022 and 2024. Emerging market bond funds have attracted more than $17 billion in net inflows this year, driven by improving sovereign credit quality, slowing inflation, and attractive real yields. While currency and geopolitical risks remain, the asset class is reemerging as a compelling fixed-income opportunity offering diversification and income.
stories.impact: Indirect but material: capital rotation into EM debt may compete with U.S. multifamily debt and equity for institutional allocations, particularly from pension funds and endowments. Rising EM real yields could pressure multifamily cap rates and debt pricing if U.S. rates remain sticky. Monitor whether this signals broader fixed-income yield compression risk in 2025, affecting construction financing and acquisition cap rates across major metros.

stories.title: Work Underway on 1,656-Bed University of Georgia Student Housing Venture
stories.excerpt: Core Spaces (Core) closed financing and broke ground on the Hub Athens Dougherty, a new 1,656-bed purpose-built student housing community located near University of Georgia set to deliver in 2028. Multifamily News reports Hub Athens Dougherty will include 536 units and 1,656 beds across a mid-rise development, offering a mix of floor plans from studios to five-bedroom units, balancing premium layouts with more affordable options to serve a wide range of student needs. Amenities include more than 27,000 square feet of interior amenities and an additional 20,000 square feet of exterior amenity space, featuring study lounges, group study rooms, fitness and wellness areas, a resort-style rooftop pool, and common spaces designed to foster connection and community. Hub Athens will also have 16,000 square feet of retail space. Key development and design partners include Mallory & Evans, JNS Realty, Northworks Architects. Construction is led by a joint venture between Core Spaces and Juneau Construction Company. Financing was provided by Affinius Capital and arranged by TSB Capital Partners. The 536-unit mid-rise development offers a range of floor plans from studios to five-bedroom units, with more than 47,000 total square feet of amenity space. Affinius Capital provided financing, arranged by TSB Capital Partners, with construction led by a joint venture between Core Spaces and Juneau Construction Company.
stories.impact: Strong capital availability for student housing in Athens market signals investor confidence in college-town multifamily demand and demographic tailwinds. 2028 delivery aligns with broader student housing supply cycle; watch for Athens market saturation risk if competing projects break ground. stories.title: The Plan: With a Big Vacancy Looming, Durst Goes Big on Renovating 114 West 47th
stories.excerpt: Situated just off Sixth Avenue is 114 West 47th Street, a 26-story office building owned by the Durst Organization that is undergoing a major renovation. By 2029, this 600,000-square-foot Midtown Manhattan office asset will be equipped with a shining new lobby, high-quality tenant amenities, private terraces on seven floors, elevators, new chillers and other building system upgrades. The building also will feature office environments with ceiling heights between 12 and 14 feet, floor plates running between 18,000 and 32,000 square feet, and an abundance of natural light. “Durst built the building in 1989, and since then U.S. Trust — which was then bought by Charles Schwab, which was then bought by Merrill Lynch, which was then bought by Bank of America — has always occupied the lion’s share of the base of the building,” said Eric Engelhardt, senior vice president of commercial leasing at Durst. “Their lease will expire in the early part of 2028, and that has prompted us to bring nearly the entire building to market.” The four office tenants and one retail tenant currently in the building will remain during the renovations. “114 West 47th Street presents a rare moment for visionary companies to position themselves in prime Midtown with a renovated, world-class work environment,” Jody Durst, president of the Durst Organization, said in a statement announcing the renovation. In the lobby, Durst and architect HOK plan to add gray granite floors and concave paneled white oak walls, as well as soft seating to provide some tranquility and calmness for those arriving from the chaos of Sixth Avenue. “The original lobby was designed in the `80s, and it was really at the pinnacle of Postmodernism, and there was a lot of multi-use of stone,” said Kenneth Drucker, design principal at HOK. “There were three formal rooms, basically an entry vestibule, and then three spaces before you got to the elevator lobby. bullets: Durst Organization renovating 114 West 47th Street, 600k sq ft Midtown Manhattan office, completing by 2029

stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, Durst's aggressive Midtown office capital deployment signals belief in office sector stabilization post-2027. If office conversion-to-residential thesis accelerates, Midtown's architectural quality (high ceilings, light, plate size) makes 114 West 47th a candidate for future residential conversion. Monitor Durst's capital allocation strategy—sustained office investment suggests conversion unlikely near-term, but watch for market signals if leasing momentum stalls post-2029.

stories.title: Bill Ackman Buys 125 West End Avenue for $260M Brain Research Institute
stories.excerpt: Billionaire hedge funder Bill Ackman has kicked off his $260 million play to establish a brain research institute on Manhattan’s Upper West Side. Pershing Square Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Ackman’s fund, dropped $188 million to acquire 125 West End Avenue, according to city documents filed Tuesday. The 400,000-square-foot life sciences building planned for the site will eventually host Ackman’s massive brain research center, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Fortune first reported. The sale by Taconic Partners reportedly precedes another in-contract sale for the neighboring building, 320 West 66th Street, for roughly $70 million. Together, the acquisitions would secure Pershing Square Foundation an estimated 700,000 square feet of research and office space between West 65th and West 66th streets. Ackman told Fortune that the charitable venture was inspired by his 26-year-old daughter, Lucy, who previously suffered a brain hemorrhage, as well as his wife, Neri Oxman, who lost her mother to Alzheimer’s disease. Pershing Square Foundation has teamed up with Mount Sinai Hospital System to develop the research institute, although the development timeline is unclear. The life sciences and office spaces at 125 West End Avenue, also called West End Labs, appear largely vacant, according to the building’s website. The building belongs to a 3.4-acre campus, known as West End Campus, sold to Taconic by Silverstein Properties for $230 million in 2019. West End Campus also includes 320 West 66th Street and a vacant parcel. Taconic repositioned the campus as a purpose-built research and laboratory complex. Its previous lives include the American Broadcasting Company (ABC)’s former campus, a Chrysler Motor Company facility and printing facilities for The New York Times. Spokespeople for Pershing Square Foundation and Taconic did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Foundation paid $188M for 125 West End Avenue, Upper West Side Manhattan

stories.summary: Pershing Square Foundation, the philanthropic arm of hedge funder Bill Ackman, acquired 125 West End Avenue on Manhattan's Upper West Side for $188 million to establish a brain research institute. The 400,000-square-foot life sciences building will eventually host the Ackman Oxman Institute. Combined with an in-contract acquisition of the neighboring 320 West 66th Street (approximately $70 million), the foundation will control an estimated 700,000 square feet of research and office space between West 65th and 66th streets.
stories.impact: Significant long-term multifamily demand signal: large-scale life sciences anchor deployment on Upper West Side drives institutional job creation, talent attraction, and population in-migration into West 65th–77th corridor. This strengthens multifamily rental demand and supports rent growth in Upper West Side and adjacent Central West Side submarkets over 3–5 years. Watch for residential conversion or new ground-up multifamily development opportunities near the campus—life sciences clusters historically catalyze young professional housing demand and allow higher rents.

stories.title: Goulston & Storrs Adds Brian Grindall to Real Estate Practice
stories.excerpt: Brian Grindall, a veteran commercial real estate attorney who spent nearly 16 years at Tenenbaum & Saas in Washington, D.C., has joined law firm Goulston & Storrs, Commercial Observer has learned. Grindall has been added to Goulston & Storrs’ real estate group as a director in the firm’s Washington, D.C., office. In addition to his time at Tenenbaum & Saas where he ascended to partner, Grindall was previously a general counsel at development firm the Opus Group, according to his Linkedin profile. “Brian has built an impressive practice advising clients on their most significant transactions,” Paul Tummonds Jr., director and administrative head of Goulston & Storrs’ D.C. office, said in a statement. “His experience, practical business perspective, and ability to navigate complex real estate matters make him an outstanding addition to our firm.” In his more than two-decade legal career, Grindall has advised CRE parties on a variety of deals including acquisitions, dispositions, financing, leasing and development. His practice also involves advising on joint ventures, loan workouts and restructuring of distressed properties. Grindall earned his master’s in real estate from Johns Hopkins University, his law degree from New England Law and his B.A. from the College of Wooster. “Goulston & Storrs has built an outstanding real estate platform and a reputation for delivering practical, business-focused counsel,” Grindall said in a statement. “I was drawn to the firm’s collaborative culture and the opportunity to work alongside a team that shares my commitment to helping clients solve complex real estate challenges.” Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Brian Grindall, 16-year veteran at Tenenbaum & Saas, joins Goulston & Storrs as director in Washington D.C. office

stories.summary: Brian Grindall, a veteran commercial real estate attorney with 16 years at Tenenbaum & Saas in Washington, D.C., and prior service as general counsel at development firm Opus Group, has joined Goulston & Storrs as a director in the firm's Washington, D.C. office. Grindall's practice covers acquisitions, dispositions, financing, leasing, development, joint ventures, and loan workouts across major commercial real estate transactions.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development strategy. However, elite law firm expansion in D.C. office market signals sustained deal velocity and complexity in the region—likely driven by multifamily and mixed-use development activity, fund formation, and institutional capital deployment. This suggests healthy transactional environment in Washington D.C. multifamily market, supporting development underwriting assumptions and financing availability for regional developers.
